speaker: (the tireman)
text: Hold your chin as if you liked the light. I have a pot and a brush. I have no use for a speech about either.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The chin is yours. The coat is the afternoon's. Edith has already had the shoulder. I am not paying a second time for a shrug.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: You are not paying once. I said so this morning, and the stitch is still a stitch. The pot is his. The hem is mine. Do not marry them in your head.

speaker: (the tireman)
text: Eyes shut. If you talk while the brush is on the lid, you will wear the word home.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I will give you no word to paint. The afternoon can have a face. It will not have a name from me in this room.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: Good. I do not sew names, and he does not paint them. There. The shrug will live. Do not roll the shoulder at the door, or you will unroll my morning.

speaker: (the tireman)
text: Open your eyes. You look like a man who is about to go on, which is what the hour is for. I am not asking which man. There are three more of you waiting, and none of you is a riddle.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then do not solve me. Leave the jaw. It is healed, and it is not a place to put colour.

speaker: edith_kettlewood
text: He will leave the jaw. Go and stand where you are meant to stand. The boy's gown is still growing, and it is still not priced, and I am not pricing it beside a brush.
